lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn introduces students to forming reported speech by reviewing changes in pronouns, tense, and sentence structure when retelling information.
Look for students identifying how direct speech changes in the examples, noticing grammar shifts, and explaining the pattern correctly.

“I have lots of friends, but they don’t all know each other. I have to tell them what everyone else wants to do! It’s not easy, but I can help them arrange something fun for the weekend. Do you know how to tell people what someone said?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - B Change the sentences into reported speech

details: Change the sentences gives focused practice converting direct quotes into accurate reported speech, reinforcing verb tense shifts, pronoun changes, and the use of that-clauses.
Look for students writing correct reported-speech sentences with proper tense backshifting and pronoun changes.
“Oh dear, all my friends are saying different things! Let’s practise changing their sentences and making the meaning clear. How quickly can you do it?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - C Read the sentences and complete the dialogues.

details: Complete the dialogues strengthens listening and reading comprehension by having students understand short sentences and transform them into reported speech in conversational form.
Look for students completing the sentence frames with correct reported speech that matches each dialogue prompt.
“Uh oh! I didn’t hear the end of the conversation. Can you be a sentence detective and complete the dialogue? I want to know what they said! Thank you very much!”
